blocks.html: It was fitting to remand the execution of the decision to the Judge of Rieux, who had not spared himself in searching out, by all honest means of Justice, the truth of this deed. Added to which, it greatly befits the dignity of the sovereign courts to maintain and preserve the authority of the inferior ones a, and so to act that, by their example and for the public good, all Judges (each in his degree) be by all and everywhere revered, as our Laws also often command b.

notes.citation: Code 7.64 (Quando provocare non est necesse), l. Omnem (fragment not identified); Decretals, X 2.28 (De appellationibus), c. Ut debitus (Lateran IV, c. 35; cf. X 2.28.59, chapter number not verified)
notes.original: l. omnẽ. C. quand. prouo non eſt nece. c. vt debitus. de appel.
notes.gloss: Ut debitus honor iudicibus et sedibus servetur — that due honour be kept to judges and their seats: the constitution restraining frivolous appeals from lower judges. The transcribers' e. for the siglum is read c., a chapter of the Decretals.

notes.citation: Digest 16.3 (Depositi vel contra), l. 1, § Casum (paragraph not verified); Digest 1.18 (De officio praesidis), l. Observandum (D. 1.18.19, Callistratus)
notes.original: l. i. P. caſum D. depoſiti l. obſeruandum D. de officio præſ.
notes.gloss: Callistratus: the magistrate dispensing justice must make himself easy of access but not suffer himself to be despised — contemni non patiatur. The transcribers' depoſt./depoſit. is the title Depositi abbreviated.

blocks.html: Afterwards, to execute the said decision, the same du Tilh was brought back from the Conciergerie to the place of Artigat, where the execution was to be done, and there was heard by the said Judge of Rieux.
